---
title: "Metric Dependence in Seasonal Heat-Stress Timing"
description: "Heat metrics can move together hour-to-hour yet identify different periods as the hottest part of the year."
status: "Manuscript in preparation"
year: 2026
---

## Research question

When heat-action planning targets the hottest part of the year, do commonly used heat-stress metrics agree on **when** that period occurs?

## Approach

Using hourly ERA5 reanalysis for India from 1980–2024, we compare the contiguous 90-day period maximizing four metrics: 2 m air temperature, Wet-Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT), Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI), and Extended Heat Index (EHI).

## Headline results

- The metrics are strongly correlated hour-to-hour, with Spearman correlations around 0.84–0.97.
- They nevertheless peak in sequence: temperature first, followed by UTCI, EHI, and WBGT.
- Over the Indo-Gangetic Plain, the median difference between temperature- and WBGT-defined heat windows is about seven weeks.
- In the hottest decile of hours, temperature and WBGT can lose essentially all rank association.
- The result suggests that choosing a heat-stress metric can also amount to choosing which part of the season is treated as most important for policy.

Figures, code, and manuscript links will be added as the paper is finalized.
